title: Volumes by the Disc and Washer Methods

questions.q: Find the volume of the solid formed by revolving $y=\sqrt{x}$ about the $x$-axis on $[0,4]$.
Find the volume of the solid formed by revolving $y=x^2$ about the $x$-axis on $[0,2]$.
Find the volume formed by revolving $x=y^2$ about the $y$-axis on $y\in[0,2]$.
Find the volume formed by revolving the region between $y=x$ and $y=x^2$ (on $[0,1]$) about the $x$-axis.
Find the volume formed by revolving the region between $y=\sqrt{x}$ and $y=x$ about the $x$-axis on $[0,1]$.
questions.answer: On $[0,1]$, $\sqrt{x}\geq x$, so outer radius $R=\sqrt{x}$, inner radius $r=x$. $V=\pi\int_0^1\left[x-x^2\right]dx=\pi\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1=\pi\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi}{6}$.

sections.heading: Volumes about a horizontal or vertical line (not an axis)

questions.q: Find the volume formed by revolving the region bounded by $y=x^2$ and $y=4$ about the line $y=4$.
questions.answer: Intersections at $x=\pm2$. Radius $=4-x^2$ (distance from curve to the line $y=4$). $V=\pi\int_{-2}^{2}\left(4-x^2\right)^2dx=\pi\int_{-2}^{2}\left(16-8x^2+x^4\right)dx=\pi\left[16x-\frac{8x^3}{3}+\frac{x^5}{5}\right]_{-2}^{2}=2\pi\left(32-\frac{64}{3}+\frac{32}{5}\right)=2\pi\cdot\frac{480-320+96}{15}=2\pi\cdot\frac{256}{15}=\frac{512\pi}{15}$.

questions.q: The base of a solid is the region between $y=x^2$ and $y=4$ on $[-2,2]$. Cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are squares. Find the volume.
questions.answer: Side length of each square $=4-x^2$. $V=\int_{-2}^{2}(4-x^2)^2\,dx=\left[16x-\frac{8x^3}{3}+\frac{x^5}{5}\right]_{-2}^{2}=2\left(32-\frac{64}{3}+\frac{32}{5}\right)=2\cdot\frac{256}{15}=\frac{512}{15}$ (same integrand as the washer-about-$y=4$ problem, but without the extra $\pi$ since cross-sections are squares, not circles).

questions.q: The base of a solid is a circle of radius $2$ ($x^2+y^2=4$). Cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are semicircles. Find the volume.
questions.answer: At each $x$, the base chord has length $2y=2\sqrt{4-x^2}$, which is the diameter of the semicircular cross-section, so its radius is $\sqrt{4-x^2}$. Semicircle area $=\frac{1}{2}\pi\left(\sqrt{4-x^2}\right)^2=\frac{\pi}{2}(4-x^2)$. $V=\int_{-2}^{2}\frac{\pi}{2}(4-x^2)\,dx=\frac{\pi}{2}\left[4x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-2}^{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}\cdot2\left(8-\frac{8}{3}\right)=\pi\cdot\frac{16}{3}=\frac{16\pi}{3}$.

questions.q: Set up (but do not evaluate) the integral for the volume of the solid whose base is the region bounded by $y=\sin x$ and the $x$-axis on $[0,\pi]$, with cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis that are equilateral triangles.
questions.answer: Each equilateral triangle has side length $s=\sin x$, so its area is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\sin^2x$. $V=\int_0^{\pi}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\sin^2x\,dx$.

sections.heading: Volume by revolving about the y-axis (washer method)

questions.q: Find the volume formed by revolving the region between $x=y^2$ and $x=2y$ about the $y$-axis.
questions.answer: Intersections: $y^2=2y \Rightarrow y(y-2)=0$: $y=0,2$. On $[0,2]$, outer radius $R=2y$, inner radius $r=y^2$. $V=\pi\int_0^2\left[(2y)^2-(y^2)^2\right]dy=\pi\int_0^2(4y^2-y^4)\,dy=\pi\left[\frac{4y^3}{3}-\frac{y^5}{5}\right]_0^2=\pi\left(\frac{32}{3}-\frac{32}{5}\right)=\pi\cdot\frac{160-96}{15}=\frac{64\pi}{15}$.
